name: MonarchFormField
title: Field
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and Row around any control, with androidx.compose.ui.semantics contentDescription and error applied to the control through a Modifier, and a polite liveRegion
summary: A visible label, one control, help text and an error message, with the label and the error given to the control for TalkBack.
whenToUse: Around a control that has no label of its own: a MonarchSwitch, a Slider, a picker, a group of buttons, or a MonarchTextField when the label should sit above the field instead of inside it.
whenNotToUse: For a plain text input MonarchTextField already has a label, helper and error. For a switch that is a whole settings row use MonarchSwitchRow.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchFormField(label: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, layout: MonarchFormFieldLayout = MonarchFormFieldLayout.Stack, enabled: Boolean = true, required: Boolean = false, helperText: String? = null, errorText: String? = null, optionalText: String? = null, errorIcon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, requiredLabel: String? = null, control: @Composable (controlModifier: Modifier) -> Unit)
public enum class MonarchFormFieldLayout { Stack, Row }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, and the TalkBack name of the control.

options.name: layout
options.description: Stack puts the label above the control; Row puts the label and help text at the start, the control at the end and the error under both.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Draws the label, mark and help text in the disabled color. Pass the same state to the control.

options.name: required
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the TalkBack name of the control.

options.name: helperText
options.description: Help text. Under the control in the stack layout, under the label in the row layout.

options.name: errorText
options.description: An error message under the field in the danger color, set as the error of the control and announced when it appears or changes. In the stack layout it replaces the help text. A blank string is no error.

options.name: optionalText
options.description: Text after the label of an optional field, such as "Optional". Ignored when required is true.

options.name: errorIcon
options.description: An icon before the error message, in the danger color. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: control
options.description: One control without a visible label of its own. It must apply the Modifier it is given, which carries the name and the error.

states.name: default
states.description: Label in the default text color with the label type, help text in the muted color with the caption type.

states.name: required
states.description: A "*" in the strong danger color after the label; "Required" is added to the name of the control.

states.name: optional
states.description: The optional text in the muted color after the label.

states.name: error
states.description: The error, with the optional icon, under the field in the strong danger color; the control is in the error state for TalkBack; announced when it appears or changes.

states.name: disabled
states.description: enabled = false draws the label, mark and help text in the disabled color; the control is disabled by the app.

appearance: Texts use the default, muted and disabled text roles and the strong danger role for the mark and the error, in every theme. The field draws no surface; the control draws its own.
platformNotes: On the web, Field gives the control its id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and aria-required through context, and NativeSelect lives in the same file. Compose has no label-for wiring, so the control slot receives a Modifier that sets the control's contentDescription to the label (with "Required") and its error semantics; the control must apply it. Compose has no described-by either, so the help text stays a readable element after the control instead of being part of the control's name; iOS puts it in the hint. The control is not told it is invalid or disabled: MonarchTextField has its own errorText parameter for its border, and enabled must be passed to the control as well. The error is announced through an always-present polite live region. The parity map lists inline-notice as a dependency; it is not used, because the error is one line of caption text under the control as on the web.
accessibility: The control is named by the label, or by the label and "Required"; the visible label and required mark are hidden from TalkBack so they are not read twice.
The error is set as the error of the control, so TalkBack reads it with the control; the visible error text is hidden from TalkBack.
A new error is announced through an always-present polite live region.
The help text is its own readable element; the error has text and an optional icon, and the required mark is backed by the spoken "Required", so neither depends on color.
In the row layout the label column comes first from the start edge, also in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: If the control does not apply the Modifier it is given, TalkBack reads the help text and the announcement but not the label on the control.
Put one control in the slot: a control made of several elements, such as a group of chips, is better given its own description.
A MonarchSwitch or MonarchCheckbox in the row layout keeps its own 48dp touch target; the label is not part of it. For a row that toggles as a whole use MonarchSwitchRow.
In the row layout the control keeps its size and the label column takes the rest, so long labels wrap.

examples.title: Validation wiring
examples.template:
MonarchFormField(
    label = {{label}},
    required = true,
    helperText = {{description}},
    errorText = if (email.isNotEmpty() && "@" !in email) {{error}} else null,
) { controlModifier ->
    MonarchTextField(
        value = email,
        onValueChange = { email = it },
        modifier = controlModifier,
        placeholder = {{placeholder}},
    )
}
examples.code:
MonarchFormField(
    label = "Email",
    required = true,
    helperText = "Used for sign-in codes only.",
    errorText = if (email.isNotEmpty() && "@" !in email) "Enter a valid email address." else null,
) { controlModifier ->
    MonarchTextField(
        value = email,
        onValueChange = { email = it },
        modifier = controlModifier,
        placeholder = "you@example.com",
    )
}

examples.title: A switch in the row layout
examples.code:
MonarchFormField(
    label = "Weekly digest",
    layout = MonarchFormFieldLayout.Row,
    helperText = "A summary of activity, sent on Monday mornings.",
) { controlModifier ->
    MonarchSwitch(checked = digest, onCheckedChange = { digest = it }, modifier = controlModifier)
}

examples.title: An error

parityExceptions.reason: The description is replaced by the error while the field is invalid, so the two are not shown together.
parityExceptions.convention: Material: the error replaces the supporting text
